business_problem: Accenture is a global professional services and consulting agency helping customers across 40 industries in more than 120 countries. Like many organizations, it had more demand than could be met by central IT, so Accenture decided to democratize and evangelize a low-code platform to empower citizen developers to solve their own problems.
solution_summary: Accenture is a global professional services and consulting agency helping customers across 40 industries in more than 120 countries. Like many organizations, it had more demand than could be met by central IT, so Accenture decided to democratize and evangelize a low-code platform to empower citizen developers to solve their own problems. Recognizing the value that Power Platform had to offer, Accenture has continued to grow its Center of Excellence, and is offering all five Microsoft Power Platform products at scale. Now, Accenture sees significant savings each year with its new model, has more than 50k newly skilled citizen developers, and has reduced IT demand for short-term applications by 30 percent, giving professional developers the ability to focus on more complex projects.

solution_components.name: Power Platform
solution_components.role: Provides the low-code platform used to build and govern internal business applications and automations.

solution_components.name: Power Apps
solution_components.role: Delivers low-code business applications that digitize workflows and data capture for end users.

solution_components.name: Power Pages
solution_components.role: Presents external-facing web experiences for partners, customers, or program participants.

solution_components.name: Power BI
solution_components.role: Publishes dashboards and reports so teams can monitor operations and act on live insights.

data_flow: This plan outlined data governance strategies, best practices, and a roadmap of when they would turn on certain capabilities and connectors to reduce shadow IT and best serve their customers.
business_outcome: Accenture often evangelizes the technology it uses to its customers, and as the biggest single user of Power Platform in the world—it wants to leverage that experience to help its customers solve their business challenges. Mathews says, “If we can stand up a new technology like Power Platform to meet the scale of Accenture it puts us in a really good position to help our clients do the same.”
metrics: Now, Accenture sees significant savings each year with its new model, has more than 50k newly skilled citizen developers, and has reduced IT demand for short-term applications by 30 percent, giving professional developers the ability to focus on more complex projects.
The company is well into its digital transformation initiative, with 90 percent of its multi-vendor IT infrastructure in the cloud.
With Power Platform, Accenture is able to fill gaps in unmet development demand and automate manual efforts, resulting in $6 million of value gained every year in avoided cost.

“For us, we define shadow IT as things we cannot see or control when we need to, so by standing up the platform and inviting our people to create and build—at its very core we have gained visibility into what people are doing and how they are connecting, which starts governance at the platform level.”

“We wanted to find a solution that would accelerate productivity and give our employees an opportunity to solve problems in real time, which low code does,” says Kate Mathews, Lead of the Accenture Power Platform Center of Excellence (CoE).
“Power Platform is so naturally interoperable with Microsoft 365, and as a top consumer of Microsoft 365 products, this was an easy place to start.”

Accenture, an early adopter of Power Platform, started its low-code journey about three years ago, driven in large part by executive sponsor Karen Odegaard identifying the need to combat the unmet demand within the central IT organization.
